question: For a basic rural roadside sign, combine Figure 2A-2 with Sections 2A.15 and 2A.16 to state the normal minimum mounting height and lateral offset.
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a basic roadside sign in a rural area, the normal minimum mounting height is 5 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement. Figure 2A-2 (drawings A and B) shows the corresponding normal lateral offset: a minimum of 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way, or a minimum of 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder where the shoulder is wider than 6 feet. Where such offsets are impractical, Section 2A.16 permits a reduced offset of at least 2 feet on certain roads. Standards (mandatory): - "In rural areas, the minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement, of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 5 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." - For context, "Where signs serve both bicyclists and other road users, vertical mounting height and lateral placement shall be as provided in Sections 2A.15 and 2A.16 of this manual." Guidance (recommended): - The figure material accompanying Section 2A.13 notes: "Lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet measured from the edge of the shoulder, or 12 feet measured from the edge of the traveled way," and refers to Section 2A.16 for lower minimums where lateral offset space is limited. Options (permitted): - "On conventional, low-volume rural, and special-purpose roads in areas where it is impractical to locate a sign with the lateral offset prescribed by this Section because of roadside features such as terrain or vegetation, a lateral offset of at least 2 feet may be used." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-2, drawing A ("Roadside sign in rural area"), shows a STOP sign with "12 ft MIN." lateral offset from the traveled way and "5 ft MIN." mounting height; drawing B shows "6 ft MIN." from the edge of a shoulder wider than 6 feet with the same "5 ft MIN." height. - [Image 2] The full page view of Figure 2A-2 confirms the same rural dimensions (12 ft MIN. lateral offset, 5 ft MIN. height) and the note referring to Section 2A.16 for reduced lateral offsets. - [Image 3] Figure 2M-3 (recreational/cultural interest area signs) shows analogous rural assembly dimensions (12 ft MIN. offset, 5 ft MIN. height) but is not the primary evidence for a basic rural roadside sign. - [Image 4] The Section 2A.15/2A.16 text page shows the mounting-height provisions and the beginning of the Lateral Offset section supporting the offset requirements. - [Image 5] Figure 2A-3 carries the note that lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder or 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way, with Section 2A.16 governing lower minimums. Citations: - Section 2A.15 Standard §4 (p.58) - Section 9A.02 Standard §4 (p.1047) - Section 2A.13 Guidance §6 (p.57) - Section 2A.16 Option §9 (p.60) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Page 92 - Page 93 - Page 100
gold_answer: The minimum mounting height is 5 feet. The normal minimum lateral offset is 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way, or 6 feet from the edge of a shoulder wider than 6 feet.
